display.purpose: Page and panel titles; the largest type in the product — there is no oversized hero.

label.purpose: Form labels, button text, table headers.

mono.purpose: Every identifier: slugs, URLs, API keys, email addresses, tabular figures.

caption.purpose: Upper micro step: uppercase console kickers, dense-table primary cells (referrer/IP/timestamp). Dense operator chrome only — never reading copy.

micro.purpose: Smallest step, one notch below Caption to subordinate labels to values in dense blocks: uppercase field micro-labels, status-pill text (ConsoleStatusBadge), mono credential IDs, config code. text-xs (12px) is the everyday small size above both.

shadows.name: elevate-ring
shadows.purpose: Base 1px theme-aware ledge (rgba(0,0,0,0.08) light / rgba(255,255,255,0.10) dark); chips, icon tiles, status pills, controls.

shadows.name: elevate-inset
shadows.purpose: Fainter inset ledge for recessed console tiles (consoleInsetClassName).

shadows.name: elevate-hairline-b / -r
shadows.purpose: Single-edge dividers replacing a literal border-bottom/right on raised sections.

shadows.name: elevate-surface-sm
shadows.purpose: Standard console panel lift (consoleSurfaceClassName): ring + contact shadow, theme-aware.

shadows.name: auth-surface-shadow
shadows.purpose: Light-only literal for the floating auth card (adds the ambient third layer); auth-border/control-shadow are the ring-only literals.

shadows.name: focus-halo
shadows.purpose: Two-part focus halo: surface-colored spacer (#fff light / background dark) then blue ring; via .dashboard-focus-ring / .auth-focus-ring.

motion.name: transition-color-shadow
motion.purpose: Inputs and links: animate only color and shadow on state change.

motion.name: transition-button
motion.purpose: Buttons: subtle multi-property transition on interaction; reduced-motion-safe.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The main action — Ink fill, near-black, confident and neutral.

components.name: Secondary Button
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 8px 16px; border: none; border-radius: 8px; background: oklch(0.97 0 0); color: oklch(0.205 0 0); font-family: var(--font-geist-sans), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s, box-shadow 0.15s; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: oklch(0.94 0 0); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #fff, 0 0 0 4px #0072f5; }

components.name: Outline Button

components.name: Ghost Button

narrative.overview: Shortly is a precision instrument for links and mail, not a marketing surface. It works like a well-machined tool: neutral, exact, and quiet at rest, so the user's own data — the URL, the slug, the click count, the incoming message — is always the loudest thing on screen. The interface earns trust by getting out of the way. Nothing is decorative; every border, weight, and shade of gray is load-bearing. The system is monochrome by discipline. It builds hierarchy from a near-black-to-white neutral ramp, hairline borders, and generous whitespace rather than from color or ornament. A single interaction blue (#0072f5) is the one chromatic voice, and it is spent almost entirely on focus and links — its rarity is exactly what makes it read as 'the system is paying attention.' Surfaces are crisp white panels floating on a soft off-white ground, lifted by a signature ring-plus-shadow that reads as physical without ever feeling glossy. The temperament is calm, credible, and low-pressure. It is light-mode first, and deliberately rejects AI-SaaS template gloss, crypto/neon hype, heavy enterprise-admin chrome, and toy-app playfulness. Motion is minimal and reduced-motion-safe: transitions confirm state, they never perform.
keyCharacteristics: Monochrome neutral ramp; color is an event, not a surface.
Geist Sans + Geist Mono; mono carries every identifier (slugs, keys, addresses).
Crisp white panels on #fafafa, lifted by a layered ring-plus-shadow.
Hairline border dividers and disciplined spacing do the structural work.
Light-mode first; quiet, exact, and reduced-motion-safe.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Interaction Blue is the only chromatic color in the interface, and it appears on a tiny fraction of any screen — focus rings, links, active states. Primary actions are Ink (near-black), not blue. If blue starts filling buttons, cards, or banners, the system has lost its voice.

rules.name: The Load-Bearing Gray Rule
rules.body: Every gray is a decision. Hierarchy comes from the neutral ramp and hairline borders, not from adding hues. Reach for another step on the ramp before reaching for color.

rules.name: The Neutral-Status Rule
rules.body: Status is carried by the label, never by hue. ConsoleTone maps every state onto the neutral ramp plus the two reserved colors: good -> bg-foreground (Ink), warning -> bg-muted-foreground, neutral -> bg-muted-foreground/45, accent -> bg-focus (the one blue), danger -> bg-destructive (the one red). There is deliberately no green success and no orange warning token; the dot is a quiet weight signal and the text states the meaning.

rules.name: The Light-Only Auth Rule
rules.body: The auth and landing surfaces are intentionally light-only and set neutrals as literal hex (#171717, #4d4d4d, #8f8f8f, #d4d4d4, bg-white) rather than theme tokens. This is a deliberate exception, not drift: do not tokenize them or wire them to the dark theme. Interaction Blue (#0072f5) stays the one accent there too.

rules.name: The Mono-For-Identifiers Rule
rules.body: If a string is copied, keyed, or machine-meaningful (slug, URL, key, address, count), it is set in Geist Mono. Prose is never mono; identifiers are never proportional.

rules.name: The Touch-Target Floor Rule
rules.body: Density is a fine-pointer concern, so compact h-8/h-9 controls keep tight sizing on desktop. A global @media (pointer: coarse) rule floors real controls (button, [role=button], a[data-slot=button], select, summary) to >=44px; prose links and checkboxes/radios are excluded. Hover-reveal affordances are gated on [@media(hover:hover)]: so they stay visible on touch.

rules.name: The Ring-First Rule
rules.body: Elevation begins with a 1px ledge (--elevate-ring), then adds soft, low-opacity ambient layers. Never a single dark blur. In light mode opacities stay <= 0.08; depth is felt, not seen. Reach for an .elevate-* utility rather than a new shadow-[...] literal.

rules.name: The Focus-Halo Rule
rules.body: Focus is a two-part halo: a spacer ring the color of the surface (--focus-gap, #fff light / background dark) then a 2px Interaction Blue ring, via .dashboard-focus-ring / .auth-focus-ring; form controls use shadcn's 3px ring with a blue border. The blue is the semantic --color-focus/bg-focus token, not --ring (which desaturates in dark). Focus is always visible and always blue; never remove it.

dos: Do keep Interaction Blue (#0072f5) reserved for focus, links, and active states; make primary actions Ink (near-black).
Do build hierarchy from the neutral ramp and hairline borders before considering any color.
Do set every identifier — slug, URL, API key, email address, count — in Geist Mono.
Do elevate surfaces with the ring-first layered shadow (0 0 0 1px + soft ambient), radius 14px for panels, 8px for controls.
Do keep focus states visible as the blue halo, and keep all motion subtle and reduced-motion-safe.
Do design light-mode first, keep the dark theme coherent, and write user-facing copy Chinese-first.
Do provide dense tables on desktop and stacked card layouts on mobile for the same data.
Do carry status meaning in the label and map status dots onto the neutral ramp plus the one blue and one red.
Do keep dense h-8/h-9 controls on fine pointers, floor real controls to >=44px on coarse pointers, and gate hover-reveal on [@media(hover:hover)]:.
Do reach for the .elevate-* utilities and --elevate-* variables for depth so surfaces stay coherent in both themes.
donts: Don't fill buttons, cards, or banners with blue, or introduce a second accent hue.
Don't use heavy single-blur drop shadows, glossy gradients, or glassmorphism — opacities stay <= 0.08.
Don't use sharp 0px corners or oversized display type; there is no marketing hero here.
Don't drift into AI-SaaS template gloss, crypto/neon hype, enterprise-admin heaviness, or toy-app playfulness.
Don't set prose in mono or identifiers in the proportional font.
Don't remove or dim focus rings, and don't rely on animation to convey meaning.
Don't add a green success or orange warning status color — status is neutral-ramp weight plus the label.
Don't tokenize or dark-theme the auth/landing hex literals; that light-only exception is intentional.
